title: Personal Pronouns
intro: Personal pronouns replace nouns to refer to people. Russian has singular pronouns (I, you, he/she/it) and plural pronouns (we, you, they). An important distinction is between informal 'ты' (you) and formal/plural 'вы' (you). Using the right form shows respect and understanding of social context.
rules: Singular pronouns: я (I), ты (you informal), он (he), она (she), оно (it).
Plural pronouns: мы (we), вы (you formal/plural), они (they).
Use ты with friends, family, children, and peers. Use вы for strangers, elders, bosses, and formal situations.
Он/она/оно match the grammatical gender of the noun, not natural gender: стол (table) → он, книга (book) → она.
examples: Ты говоришь по-русски? (Do you speak Russian? - informal)
Вы говорите по-русски? (Do you speak Russian? - formal)
Он читает. Она читает. (He reads. She reads.)

items.explanation: Я is the first person singular pronoun, meaning 'I'.
Мы is the first person plural pronoun, meaning 'we'.
Они is the third person plural pronoun, meaning 'they'.

items.prompt: You're talking to your boss. Which 'you' do you use?
items.promptEnglish: You're talking to your boss. Which 'you' do you use?
items.hint: Formal situations require the polite form
items.explanation: Use вы (formal 'you') when speaking to bosses, elders, or strangers.

items.prompt: Which form of 'you' would you use with a close friend?
items.promptEnglish: Which form of 'you' would you use with a close friend?
items.explanation: Use ты (informal 'you') with friends, family, and children.

items.prompt: The word «книга» is feminine. Which pronoun replaces it?
items.promptEnglish: The word 'книга' is feminine. Which pronoun replaces it?
items.hint: Feminine nouns use the feminine pronoun
items.explanation: Она (she/it) replaces feminine nouns like книга.
